comment: French narration pronunciation pins (BRIEF section 9), applied by audio/tts.py to films built with --lang fr (whole words, case-sensitive, longest key first). Fish Audio phoneme pins are English-only, so every French pin is a respelling {"say": ...} that a French reader pronounces the way a French physicist says the word: acronyms spelled in French letters (ème, hache, dé...), names said the French way, Gissinger in French (BRIEF D12). {"keep": true} entries are documentation only: the word stays as written, e.g. the English machine-learning terms that French researchers say in English (the multilingual voice reads them in English; 'alt' is the respelling to try if a take sounds wrong). Changing an entry re-synthesises (and re-bills) only the French paragraphs that contain the word. Entries listed in 'check' want the user's or the supervisors' confirmation. Supervisors' names are not narrated (BRIEF D6).

VKS.note: von Kármán Sodium, spelled in French

DRESDYN.note: DREsden DYNamo, read as a word

SFEMaNS.note: S-FEMaNS: S spelled, then FEMaNS read as a word

LATU.note: read as a word, French 'la-tu' (or spelled L-A-T-U?)

Rice.note: formule de Rice, said as in English 'rice'

Rm.note: the symbol Rm, read in French letters

Pm.note: the symbol Pm, read in French letters

flow matching.note: kept in English, as French ML researchers say it

Jensen.note: inégalité de Jensen: French readers say 'jin-sène' or 'djènn-sènn'; to confirm
